title: Latch-based timing methodology with cycle stealing
where_in_paper: Likely timing methodology / circuit style discussion, but I cannot recall the exact section
decision: Use transparent-latch timing and allow local time borrowing / cycle stealing rather than treating every path as a strict edge-triggered pipeline stage.
alternatives_or_rejected: A purely edge-triggered style would simplify hold and static-timing analysis, but it would remove the ability to borrow time across adjacent pipeline stages.
rationale: Latch-based cycle stealing can absorb path imbalance and local variation, helping a high-frequency design close timing without paying the full penalty on every locally slow path.
outcome: This would make timing closure more flexible but would require careful latch-aware timing analysis and hold control. I am not confident the paper gives a specific quantitative outcome.

title: On-chip power-grid and decap planning for supply noise
where_in_paper: Likely power distribution / physical design section, but exact section recall is weak
decision: Provide substantial on-chip power distribution and local decoupling capacitance rather than relying primarily on package and board decoupling.
alternatives_or_rejected: Using less on-chip decap or a lighter power mesh would preserve routing resources and area, but would increase IR drop and transient supply droop.
rationale: A high-current, high-frequency microprocessor needs low-resistance distribution and local charge storage to keep supply noise within timing and reliability limits.
outcome: Supply noise is treated as a first-order physical-design constraint. I do not confidently recall the paper stating exact numerical results.

title: Hierarchical partitioning between custom and automated blocks
where_in_paper: Likely physical design organization / floorplan discussion, but exact section recall is weak
decision: Partition the large chip hierarchically, applying custom or semi-custom effort to performance-critical macros while using more automated implementation elsewhere.
alternatives_or_rejected: A uniform standard-cell approach would improve productivity but might miss critical performance targets; a fully custom approach would be too expensive in design effort and schedule.
rationale: The chip was too large and performance-sensitive to close with a single homogeneous methodology; hierarchy localizes critical work and timing convergence.
outcome: The design obtained a compromise between custom performance and productivity. I am not confident the paper quantifies the exact partition or effort split.
